title: Empire of Japan
capsule: The Empire of Japan dates from the Meiji Restoration of January 1868, when the Tokugawa shogunate was overthrown and the emperor Meiji was restored to formal sovereignty; rapid industrialization, conscript armies, and constitutional government under the Meiji Constitution of 1889 transformed Japan into a major industrial and military power within a generation. Victory against China (1894–1895) yielded Taiwan and influence in Korea; the Russo-Japanese War (1904–1905) confirmed Japan as the dominant power in East Asia and brought the Liaodong Peninsula and railway rights in Manchuria. Japan's continental expansion accelerated with the Manchurian Incident (1931), full-scale war with China from 1937, and Pacific War from December 1941; defeat by Allied forces and atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki (6 and 9 August 1945) ended the empire, and Japan formally surrendered on 2 September 1945.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Metropolitan Japanese territory and formal colonial possessions (Taiwan, Korea, Karafuto, Kwantung Leased Territory, South Sea Mandate) are precisely attested by colonial administrative records and treaty documents; the extent of occupied territories in China and Southeast Asia during 1937–1945 is well-documented by military and administrative sources though the operational front lines shifted continuously.
